body.statement: Let \(K\) be an ordered subfield of \(\mathbb R\). Given effective arithmetic and sign oracles for \(K\), let a semialgebraic set in \(N\) variables be described by a Boolean combination of sign conditions on \(s\) polynomials of degree at most \(d\) over \(K\). Sign determination, quantifier elimination, real-univariate sampling, cylindrical decomposition, and roadmap algorithms decide emptiness, compute projections and semialgebraically connected-component descriptions, and return sample points meeting all components. Exact outputs can be represented by square-free univariate polynomials over \(K\), rational functions of a selected root, and Thom signs. For fixed \((N,s,d)\) these procedures terminate, and their arithmetic, degree, and integer-input bit complexity admit effective bounds obtained from the projection, sampling, and roadmap recurrences.
